description: §6.7.7 / §42.2.4 — a `<request>`-ref member as an `is`-predicate LHS inside a VALUE / BOOLEAN / CLASS attribute (`disabled=<#userReq>.data is some`, `class=<#userReq>.data is some ? …`, `value=<#userReq>.data is some`, `class:on=<#userReq>.data is some`). Regression pin for g-request-is-some-in-value-bool-class-attr (the value/bool/class siblings of the S312 `if=`-attr fix). Pre-fix these miscompiled to `_scrml_input_state_registry.get("userReq").(data !== null && ...)` — the boolean attr aborted the whole compile with E-CODEGEN-INVALID-LOGIC (no client bundle written), and the value/plain-class attr was silently DROPPED (W-CG-VALUE-ATTR-UNLOWERABLE) because the lowerability probe mangled the same escape-hatch. Codes-half: all four forms must compile (no E-CODEGEN-INVALID-LOGIC). Runtime-half: on a 2xx settle `<#userReq>.data is some` becomes true, so #btn gains `disabled`, #box's class becomes `ready`, and #fld's live `.value` becomes `true` — all driven by the always-on `_scrml_effect` the bool/value emitters wrap. Twin of request-data-is-some-if-attr-rt on the attribute-value / boolean / class paths (the `if=` path was already correct at S312).
rationale: §42.2.4: `<lhs> is some` lowers to a presence check over the WHOLE lhs; the `<#id>` request-ref sigil is a valid lhs base and its member (`.data`) must route to the reactive `_scrml_request_<id>` object (§6.7.7), not the §36 input-state registry which a request never populates. Every attribute callsite (value-attr lowerability probe, reactive-bool-attr toggle, reactive-value-attr write, class: directive) must re-parse the `<#`-leading escape-hatch and thread requestIds so it lowers IDENTICALLY to the `if=` / `${...}` text-interpolation paths.
